brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three hex piece cells at axial (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) on level 0, a straight row, joined by joint bolts (lockJoints).
addBin hex-bin-full-drain at (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) — one bin per cell.

The bins are the 'drained' full-depth variant (hex-bin-full-drain), which the catalog defines with drainage holes. I cannot verify the hole geometry beyond the part name, and a drain hole in a printed tray does not prove water-tightness or drainage performance.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell row of hex cells, each holding a full-depth drained bin, with open faces capped and joints locked. Each bin is filled with soil and planted (basil, mint, thyme, young stage). check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. Material suitability (outdoor, watering, food contact) is not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
